'''Valentina Harizanov''' is a [[Serbian-American]] [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at [[The George Washington University]].  Her main research contributions are in [[computable model theory|computable structure theory]] (roughly at the intersection of [[computability theory]] and [[model theory]]), where she introduced the notion of degree spectra of relations on computable structures and obtained the first significant results concerning uncountable, countable, and finite [[Turing degree]] spectra.<ref name="Harizanov1987">{{cite journal
 | author = Harizanov, V.S.
 | year = 1987
 | title = Degree Spectrum of a Recursive Relation on a Recursive Structure
 | journal = Ph.D. Dissertation, University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison
}}</ref>     Her recent interests include [[algorithmic learning theory]] and spaces of [[partial order|order]]s on [[group (mathematics)|group]]s.

== Education ==
She obtained her Bachelor of Science in mathematics in 1978 at the [[University of Belgrade]] and her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1987 at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] under the direction of [[Terry Millar]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=10240}}</ref><ref name=cv>{{cite web |url=https://home.gwu.edu/~harizanv/vharizanovcv.pdf |access-date=15 January 2018 |website=[[The George Washington University]] |title=Curriculum Vitae of Valentina Harizanov }}</ref>

== Career ==
At The George Washington University, Harizanov was an [[assistant professor]] of mathematics from 1987 to 1993, an [[associate professor]] of mathematics from 1994 to 2002, and a professor of mathematics from 2003 to the present.
She has held two [[visiting professor]] positions, one in 1994 at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] and one in 2014 at the Kurt Gödel Research Center at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref name=cv/>

Harizanov has co-directed the Center for Quantum Computing, Information, Logic, and Topology at The George Washington University since 2011.<ref name=cv/>

== Research ==
In 2009, Harizanov received a grant from the [[National Science Foundation]] to research how algebraic, topological, and algorithmic properties of mathematical structures relate.<ref name=nsf>{{cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0904101 |website=[[National Science Foundation]] |title=Award Abstract #0904101: Topics in Computable Mathematics |access-date=15 January 2018 }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Harizanov won the Oscar and Shoshana Trachtenberg Prize for Faculty Scholarship from The George Washington University (GWU) in 2016.<ref name=prize>{{cite web |url=https://facultyaffairs.gwu.edu/trachtenberg-research-award-winners |title=Trachtenberg Research Award Winners |website=[[The George Washington University]] |access-date=15 January 2018}}</ref>
This award is presented each year to a [[tenure]]d GWU faculty member to recognize outstanding research accomplishments.<ref name="prize-desc">{{cite web |url=https://facultyaffairs.gwu.edu/oscar-and-shoshana-trachtenberg-prize-faculty-scholarship-research |title=Oscar and Shoshana Trachtenberg Prize for Faculty Scholarship (Research) |website=[[The George Washington University]] |access-date=15 January 2018 |archive-date=16 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116135447/https://facultyaffairs.gwu.edu/oscar-and-shoshana-trachtenberg-prize-faculty-scholarship-research |url-status=dead }}</ref> She was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Eisenbud Professor for Fall 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Harizanov has over 40 publications in [[peer-review]]ed journals, including
*V.S. Harizanov, "Some effects of Ash-Nerode and other decidability conditions on degree spectra " Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 55 (1), pp.&nbsp;51&ndash;65 (1991), cited 21 times according to [[Web of Science]]

In addition, she has published the following book-length survey paper and co-edited, co-authored book:

*V.S. Harizanov, “Pure computable model theory,” in the volume: Handbook of Recursive Mathematics, vol. 1, Yu.L. Ershov, S.S. Goncharov, A. Nerode, and J.B. Remmel, editors (North-Holland, Amsterdam, 1998), pp.&nbsp;3&ndash;114.
*M. Friend, N.B. Goethe, and V.S. Harizanov, Induction, Algorithmic Learning Theory, and Philosophy, Series: Logic, Epistemology, and the Unity of Science, vol. 9, Springer, Dordrecht, 304 pp., 2007.

Degree spectra of relations are introduced and first studied in Harizanov's dissertation: ''Degree Spectrum of a Recursive Relation on a Recursive Structure''(1987).<ref name=Harizanov1987/>
